With the new finer-grained locking, two callers that race through `getOrCreateIndex` for the same key when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold` will both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory. bleve's New on an already-existing directory either errors or reopens stale state; one call returns an error to a caller even though the index they wanted was successfully created and is sitting in the cache. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` already has a TODO admitting it has no per-key mutex, so this relaxation of the backend's serialization makes a known race easier to trigger. The `errgroup` already sets the search index up; now the broadcaster independently starts a second poller querying the same resource history tables. Two pollers every 100 ms doubles DB load, doubles history scans, and produces two independent `mostRecentRV` writers and two event streams. findings.title: BuildIndex loses per-key serialization, allowing same-key races
findings.body: The diff removes `b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()` from the top of `BuildIndex` and only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Previously, two concurrent calls to `BuildIndex` for the same `key` were serialized, so `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` (lines ~96-102) was only ever invoked once per directory. With the new finer-grained locking, two callers that race through `getOrCreateIndex` for the same key when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold` will both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory. bleve's New on an already-existing directory either errors or reopens stale state; one call returns an error to a caller even though the index they wanted was successfully created and is sitting in the cache. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` already has a TODO admitting it has no per-key mutex, so this relaxation of the backend's serialization makes a known race easier to trigger. Consider keeping the exclusive lock around the directory creation (or adding a per-key `sync.Map` / singleflight) and only using the finer-grained lock to protect the cache map mutation.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` does `for _, v := range b.cache { ... }` with no read-lock on `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under `cacheMu`. Go map iteration concurrent with writes panics with "concurrent map iteration and map write". The new `s.log.Info(..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` added in `search.go` happens after `group.Wait()` so it is safe today, but `TotalDocs` is part of the `SearchBackend` interface and any future caller (e.g., a metrics endpoint, health check, or test) that invokes it while index construction is in flight will crash the process. Either take `cacheMu.RLock()` for the iteration, or iterate a snapshot of the keys under the lock.

findings.title: Two long-running WatchWriteEvents pollers run for the same backend
findings.body: After this change, both `searchSupport.init` (lines ~202-213 in search.go) and `server.initWatcher` (line 752) each call `s.backend.WatchWriteEvents(...)`, which for the SQL backend (`pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:558`) starts its own 100 ms poller goroutine. The `errgroup` already sets the search index up; now the broadcaster independently starts a second poller querying the same resource history tables. Two pollers every 100 ms doubles DB load, doubles history scans, and produces two independent `mostRecentRV` writers and two event streams. The order swap (initWatcher first vs. search.init first) does not change this — both sequences still leave the search support's watcher running alongside `initWatcher`. The author's stated goal was just to parallelize index build across distinct keys; the duplicate watcher is unrelated and should be removed (let the search support's handler pipe into the broadcaster, or use the broadcaster as the single event source).

findings.title: Postgres integration test now silently skipped with a TODO
findings.body: The diff adds `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }` to the only integration test that exercises the storage server target with a real DB. Combined with the existing `sqlite3` skip, the test is now skipped for every DB type the CI matrix runs against — it provides no coverage. The TODO comment admits the test "works locally" but not in Drone, strongly suggesting the new eager `Init()` in `NewResourceServer` exposes an init-only failure mode that the lazy initialization hid. A `t.Skip` is the wrong fix here: the test should be made to pass for both `Init()` orderings, or split so that the storage-server integration is verified separately for postgres. Otherwise a regression in the eager-init path on postgres will land unnoticed.

findings.title: Eager Init swallows cancelation from the caller's context
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now passes its locally constructed `ctx` (a `context.WithCancel(context.Background(), ...)` wrapping a static service-account identity) into `s.Init(ctx)`. Inside `Init`, this `ctx` is forwarded to `search.init(ctx)`, which in turn calls `s.storage.GetResourceStats(ctx, ...)` and `s.storage.ListIterator(ctx, ...)` for every namespace being indexed. Those calls now use a context that lives for the lifetime of the server and is only cancelled when `s.Stop` runs — they never see a deadline or the caller's cancellation. That is fine for a production server, but `NewResourceServer` is also called from `InitializeModuleServer` in tests and from any tooling that builds a transient server. The previous per-handler `s.Init(ctx)` propagated the per-request deadline/cancellation, so a hung DB could be aborted by closing the test context. With the eager call, an unresponsive backend during index build will block `NewResourceServer` indefinitely, which in turn blocks module startup with no way to cancel it from outside.
